title: Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract Terms: Changing the Monthly Due Date
content:
**Contract servicing terms, Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract — due-date changes.**

1. A due-date change can be made only while the contract status is active.
2. The contract must show 0 days past due, installments satisfied of at least the tier's minimum for a due-date change, and due-date changes used below the tier's lifetime maximum.
3. A due-date change may take effect no earlier than the tier's interval in calendar months after the last due-date change took effect. The interval is counted in calendar months from the last due-date change date recorded on the contract to the same day number of the later month, falling back to that month's last day when the day does not exist; a contract that has never changed its due date has no interval to wait.
4. The new due day must lie between the tier's earliest and latest due day of the month, and the first installment on the new due day may fall no more than the tier's maximum shift in calendar days after the current next due date and never before it.
5. **Exception — relationship alignment.** A change whose new due day equals the due day of another open Kestrel retail, pre-owned or balloon contract, or of an active Kestrel lease, of the same customer is a relationship alignment and does not have to wait for the interval; it still counts toward the lifetime maximum.
6. No fee is charged; simple interest continues to accrue daily, so a longer gap to the first installment on the new due day increases the interest portion of that installment.
7. The change updates the due day, the next due date, the count of due-date changes used and the last due-date change date on the contract; the maturity date moves to the new due day in the final month.

## The interval as a time test

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| Clock starts from | the last due-date change date recorded on the contract |
| Counting | calendar months to the same day number of the later month; the month's last day where that day does not exist |
| Comparison | the new change takes effect not earlier than the end of the interval |
| Boundary | taking effect on the anniversary day itself is permitted |
| No prior change | no interval applies |

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, 12-month interval):* after a change dated 15 March of one year, a change may take effect on 15 March of the next year, but not on 14 March. After a change dated 29 February of a leap year, a 12-month interval ends on 28 February of the following year, the last day of that month.

*Alignment (hypothetical):* a customer whose active Kestrel lease is due on the 12th asks to move this contract's due day to the 12th eight months after a previous change; the change need not wait for the interval, and it counts as one of the lifetime changes.
